problem: The design of priority.dev rests on guesses. No one has measured whether a small model gives valid, grounded output on real transcripts. No one has seen what the hooks and tmux do in a live session. Ten rounds of design produced documents and no measurement.
why_now: The design has converged, the models are chosen, and the key is in place. Building the policy and the actuator on a guess would be costly to undo.
approach: A spike program in priority-dev/, built with /implement:start: 4 epics and 13 slices, probes first. The probes are a model probe, a hook probe, and a tmux probe. Then come the stop brief, Interpret, Digest, and the replay report, then the event log, then the adapter to the log. Each unknown is a criterion in a blind rubric. Three merges apply: call records, a hook timeout with a bypass file, and failure drills that end in Abstain. After slice 7 the engineer decides go or no-go. The spike uses no Jev.

alternatives.option: A deterministic interpreter with no model, from hook fields and regex
alternatives.rejected_because: It retires no model unknown, and it breaks the decision to use Nemo and Inkling. A hand-labelled rule baseline may come later.

alternatives.option: An evidence-grade hash chain over every record, with signed checkpoints
alternatives.rejected_because: Nobody audits a spike, and the chain delays the first slices. The model id, prompt hash, and raw reply are kept without a chain.

alternatives.option: The event log envelope first, as the only durable contract
alternatives.rejected_because: The envelope shape depends on real hook payloads and transcript lag, which the probes measure. The log therefore comes after the probes.

alternatives.option: One 60-line script as the whole spike
alternatives.rejected_because: It skips the hook and tmux unknowns, which need a live session. It is kept as slice 1 only.

alternatives.option: A claims.yaml ledger file with pass lines
alternatives.rejected_because: A hidden blind rubric already carries each measure, and a second file would drift from it. The engineer chose the rubrics.

alternatives.option: A pd command-line tool and a runbook inside the spike
alternatives.rejected_because: They add polish before the unknowns are measured. Only the hook timeout and the bypass file are kept.

alternatives.option: Keep the first draft order: interpreter first, hook slices last
alternatives.rejected_because: The hook and tmux results change how the adapter works, so late probes risk rework. The engineer asked for them early.

out_of_scope: Jev, the policy, the actuator, the attention queue, and the notifier
A second harness such as Pi, and the launch of new sessions
Optimisers and retry modules for DSPy
A real priority-dev-phase-a program, which waits for its own design
risks: Nemo may fail on the nested action payloads. The calls are small, and code checks every quote, so a failure ends as an Abstain
The free tier of Inkling may rate-limit a goal run. The replay report counts the limit errors
A hook that waits may freeze a live session. Every hook has a timeout and a bypass file
Real transcripts hold secrets. Fixtures stay local, git ignores them, and redaction runs before any model call
A probe slice can pass at 0.90 and still refute its claim. The rubric checks that the report is honest and complete, not that the number is good
The OpenRouter calls to Nemo are paid, though cheap. A replay over many stops needs a spend cap
The event log needs Docker and Postgres on the development machine
testing: Each slice has a blind rubric. A criterion is an unknown with an observable answer
The modules run in tests with a dummy model, and the replay uses the real models on the local fixtures
The probes run in a scratch tmux session with a scratch Claude Code session, never in a live one
A contract test covers the event log append, the idempotency key, and the cursor
reviewer_focus: Does the order retire the largest unknown first, and does each slice end in a state a command shows
Does the stop brief rename leave any old use of slice for the interpreter input
Does the bypass file release a session in every failure of the hook
unknowns: Whether Nemo returns valid Fill JSON for most of the 13 action kinds
Whether $TMUX_PANE reaches a hook, and how long the transcript lags after Stop
Whether the permission dialog shows while a PermissionRequest hook waits
Whether a paste into a busy pane is lost
Whether the free tier of Inkling sustains the event rate of 5 sessions
What the transcript holds when a /goal clears
